Excellencies, distinguished delegates, I call to order our resumed session, second plenary meeting, which is being held in, in public. The Assembly of States Parties is mindful of the considerable interest of the disciplinary proceedings involving an elected official upon which the Assembly has taken a decision today. At the outset, I wish to thank all delegates for their constructive approach and for their close consideration of the 8th of June decision of the Bureau, the OIOS investigative report and underlying evidence, the Panel report, the submissions of the Prosecutor to the Panel and to the Bureau, and the submissions of VO1 to the Bureau. Which were the foundational material upon which the Assembly decision has been taken. In that regard, I emphasize that the Bureau and the Assembly of States Parties have decided this matter within the context in which it is. It is an international— an internal workplace complaint of prohibited conduct by an elected official against a subordinate staff member. The Bureau of the Assembly of States Parties have taken their decisions in full adherence to the legal framework of the International Criminal Court and with full respect for the due process rights of the elected official and the rights of the affected persons. The Assembly has decided by majority of 82 States Parties that the elected official prosecutor Karim Khan committed serious misconduct and a serious breach of duty under Article 46 of the Rome Statute, and to remove the elected official prosecutor Karim Khan from office under Article 46, paragraph 2 of the Rome Statute. Prior to closing this plenary session, I wish to underscore that within the legal framework of the International Criminal Justice Criminal Court, complaints of misconduct investigations and disciplinary proceedings are confidential matters. I continue to call for respect for the dignity and privacy of all those involved. In closing, I express my deep appreciation to the Assembly of States Parties for their diligent consideration of this difficult matter and for the spirit of unity shown in upholding the integrity of the Court. I acknowledge the dedication of the Court staff, who have continued to work tirelessly in the implementation of the Court's critical mandate. During this prolonged period of uncertainty. While the Court may have more challenges ahead, the Assembly's navigation of this difficult matter, coupled with the dedication of the Court staff and elected officials, has demonstrated the resolve to continue to support the Court through difficult times and to ensure that it can discharge its critical mandate. in the interests of the international community as a whole and victims of atrocity crimes the world over.
